source_records.normalized_excerpt: On May 19, 2016, SBI Holdings announced that it and Ripple Labs jointly established SBI Ripple Asia Co., Ltd. to develop and provide a next-generation blockchain-based payment platform for Japan and the wider Asian region.

On September 16, 2016, SBI Holdings and its wholly owned subsidiary SBI Investment announced an additional investment in Ripple Labs. SBI's release states the $55 million third-party financing round included SBI's FinTech Fund, Standard Chartered Bank and Siam Commercial Bank.

On October 21, 2016, SBI Ripple Asia relayed Ripple's announcement of an R3 interbank cross-border settlement trial using XRP with 12 consortium banks. The release describes a trial/proof of concept, not production deployment by those banks.

SBI's 2023 release states that SBI Remit began a Japan-to-Philippines international remittance service using XRP as the bridge currency in 2021, and in September 2023 expanded XRP-based bank-account remittances to the Philippines, Vietnam and Indonesia. SBI VC Trade sends XRP in response to SBI Remit's customer remittance request; Tranglo and local partners enable recipients to receive local fiat.

SBI VC Trade states that in July 2021 it built the system for SBI Remit's Japan-to-Philippines service using Ripple's On-Demand Liquidity solution and XRP as a bridge currency; in July 2022 it renewed the system as a multi-tenant service to connect multiple remittance providers and crypto exchanges.

SBI's 2025 investor presentation states that SBI Group held approximately 9% of Ripple shares as the largest external shareholder at the presentation date; this is a dated holding disclosure, not a guarantee of the current percentage.
SBI Group's corporate profile states that SBI Group held 82.96% of SBI Remit's voting rights as of August 28, 2026; SBI Remit is therefore a controlled group company but not 100% owned by the group.

On February 20, 2026, SBI Ripple Asia announced a technical-support partnership with Asia Web3 Alliance Japan to help startups implement blockchain-based financial services, with XRPL identified as the contemplated blockchain.

On February 26, 2026, SBI Ripple Asia announced a conceptual proof of concept for tokenized deposits and deposit-based digital money using existing SBI MoneyTap domestic-remittance infrastructure and SBI Ripple Asia's token-issuance platform, with XRPL as the contemplated blockchain.

On February 24, 2026, SBI Ripple Asia and DSRV Labs began joint research on blockchain-based cross-border payment services for Japan and South Korea, with XRPL as the contemplated blockchain and stablecoin issuers as potential connected participants.
On August 22, 2025, SBI Holdings announced establishment of a joint venture with Circle Internet Holdings to promote USDC use and Web3/digital-finance use cases in Japan.

SBI VC Trade, a consolidated subsidiary of SBI Holdings, launched general USDC trading in Japan on March 26, 2025 after obtaining the first Japanese electronic-payment-instrument exchange registration on March 4, 2025.
On June 9, 2025, SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank announced strategic purchases of Circle shares at its IPO totaling $50 million: $25 million by SBI Holdings and $25 million by SBI Shinsei Bank.
Circle announced on June 12, 2025 that native USDC was live on the XRP Ledger mainnet, with Circle Mint and Circle APIs supporting USDC on XRPL; no bridge is required.

On August 22, 2025, SBI Holdings, SBI VC Trade, Ripple Labs and Ripple subsidiary Standard Custody & Trust Company announced an MOU to distribute RLUSD in Japan. SBI VC Trade initially targeted general availability during the fiscal year ending March 31, 2026.

On June 24, 2026, SBI VC Trade and Ripple announced RLUSD trading availability in SBI VC Trade's VCTRADE service, with free deposits and withdrawals; the release identifies RLUSD as a Japanese category-4 electronic payment instrument.

On July 7, 2026, SBI VC Trade reported more than two million registered accounts and said it began handling JPYSC and RLUSD in June 2026, in addition to USDC which it began offering in March 2025. Registered accounts are not the same as active stablecoin users or transaction volume.

Circle's SEC registration statement says that in August 2023 it acquired Coinbase's remaining 50% interest in Centre for approximately 8.4 million Circle common shares valued at $209.9 million; Centre became an indirect wholly owned Circle subsidiary and was dissolved in December 2023. The restructuring gave Coinbase a minority equity stake in Circle while Circle retained sole governance of the Circle stablecoin network.

Under the Collaboration Agreement with Coinbase, Coinbase receives allocations based on the amount of USDC held on its platform after Circle's issuer retention, and half of the remaining amount tied to broader ecosystem growth after approved third-party ecosystem participants. Circle incurred $331.3 million in distribution costs in connection with its agreements with Coinbase in Q3 2026 and $986.6 million in the first nine months of 2026. At September 30, 2026, USDC in circulation was $73.879 billion at period end and $73.264 billion on average; Circle's own platform held $13.868 billion, or 18.1% daily weighted-average share.

Coinbase's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q says it renewed its arrangement with Circle on the same terms, average USDC held in Coinbase products reached an all-time high, and higher average USDC balances increased stablecoin revenue by $84.6 million in Q3 and $201.6 million year-to-date, partly offset by lower average interest rates. Coinbase separately reported $8.616 billion of USDC on its own balance sheet at September 30, 2026; this is company-held USDC, not a customer balance total.

On July 8, 2026, SBI Securities, Daiwa Securities, SBI Digital Markets, Penguin Securities and BOOSTRY announced a proof of concept for cross-border securities-token circulation using Ethereum and USDC, identifying practical legal, operational and technical issues.

On October 30, 2026, SBI Holdings and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group signed a capital and business alliance to jointly study new financial services using stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets; the announcement does not specify XRP, USDC or RLUSD as an exclusive instrument.
XRPL documentation states that every transaction destroys a small XRP fee; the minimum standard reference fee is 10 drops, subject to load and transaction type.
XRPL documentation states that accounts and ledger objects require XRP reserves, currently a 1 XRP base reserve and 0.2 XRP per owner object.

XRPL sponsored-fees-and-reserves lets an account sponsor cover transaction fees and reserve requirements for another account, so an end user may not need to hold XRP directly even though the sponsor funds the XRP costs.

asset_and_ledger_distinctions.XRP: Native cryptoasset. SBI Remit uses it as a bridge currency in specific production remittance corridors; XRPL fees and reserves are also XRP-denominated.
asset_and_ledger_distinctions.XRPL: Ledger/protocol. Tokenized deposits and USDC can use XRPL without using XRP as the bridge asset.
asset_and_ledger_distinctions.USDC: Circle-issued USD stablecoin. Native on XRPL since June 12, 2025; no bridge required.
asset_and_ledger_distinctions.RLUSD: Ripple-issued USD stablecoin distributed by SBI VC Trade in Japan since June 24, 2026.
asset_and_ledger_distinctions.JPYSC: Yen stablecoin handled by SBI VC Trade; issuer/settlement details are outside this artifact's verified scope.
asset_and_ledger_distinctions.Ethereum_USDC: Separate SBI-led cross-border securities-token POC, demonstrating multi-chain strategy.

relationship_interpretation.sbi_ripple: Direct relationship: SBI invested in Ripple, reported approximately 9% as of February 2025, and co-established SBI Ripple Asia. Separately, SBI Remit uses XRP as a bridge asset in specific production corridors since 2021.
relationship_interpretation.sbi_circle: Direct relationship: SBI and Circle established a Japanese JV; SBI Holdings and SBI Shinsei Bank separately announced $50M total Circle IPO share purchases; SBI VC Trade distributes USDC.
relationship_interpretation.sbi_rlusd: Direct distribution relationship: SBI VC Trade distributes Ripple's RLUSD in Japan after an MOU with Ripple and Standard Custody.
relationship_interpretation.coinbase_circle: Direct economic relationship: Coinbase is a USDC distributor and Circle equity holder; Circle's Q3 2026 filing reports $331.3M Q3 and $986.6M nine-month distribution costs associated with Coinbase agreements.
relationship_interpretation.circle_ripple: The sources establish Circle USDC native on XRPL, not a direct Circle-Ripple corporate partnership.
relationship_interpretation.coinbase_ripple: The sources in this graph do not establish a direct Coinbase-Ripple corporate partnership. Coinbase Ventures and SBI Group share Soter as an investee at different Series B closes, which is not a direct partnership.
relationship_interpretation.sbi_strategy: SBI's strategy is multi-rail and multi-chain: XRP ODL remittances, XRPL tokenized-deposit research, USDC and RLUSD distribution, JPYSC, Ethereum/USDC securities-token POC, and a separate stablecoin/RWA alliance with SMFG.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI-linked XRP remittances create actual XRP bridge-asset utility.
competing_hypotheses.support: SBI's 2023 release identifies XRP as bridge currency and names the SBI VC Trade and Tranglo roles.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: Corridor volumes, XRP inventory turnover, realized spreads and total XRP consumed are not disclosed; no price-impact estimate is supported.

competing_hypotheses.claim: XRPL stablecoin/tokenized-deposit growth could increase XRP fee/reserve use.
competing_hypotheses.support: XRPL fees are paid/burned in XRP and reserves are XRP-denominated.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: USDC and tokenized deposits do not require XRP as bridge asset; sponsored fees/reserves can shift the XRP requirement to sponsors; no fee-volume attribution is measured here.

competing_hypotheses.claim: SBI is strategically aligned with XRP/XRPL.
competing_hypotheses.support: SBI Ripple Asia JV, Ripple equity investment, SBI Remit ODL and RLUSD distribution.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: SBI also distributes USDC/JPYSC, invested in Circle, studies Ethereum/USDC, and partners with SMFG on broader stablecoin/RWA services.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Coinbase and Circle are economically aligned.
competing_hypotheses.support: Equity consideration from Centre restructuring, ongoing distribution agreement and Q3 2026 distribution costs.
competing_hypotheses.counterevidence: Circle retains sole stablecoin-network governance; Coinbase's current exact ownership percentage and net agreement economics are not fully disclosed in these excerpts.

reasons: Corporate relationships and announced POCs are event context, not measured XRP order flow.
Only SBI Remit's bridge-asset use is explicitly XRP-specific; transaction volumes and dates of individual XRP purchases are absent.
XRPL tokenized-deposit and USDC integrations must not be mislabeled as XRP bridge demand.
Circle/Coinbase distribution costs and USDC circulation are ecosystem metrics, not direct XRP demand.
